name: Australia
snapshot: Pauline Hanson's One Nation overtook the Liberals in the polls in 2026, cracking Australia's two-party system even as Labor kept its lead head to head.
culture: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have the world's oldest continuous cultures, stretching back more than 60,000 years. Modern Australia is highly multicultural, with nearly a third of residents born overseas. Beach life, barbecues, Aussie rules football, cricket and rugby league are national pastimes. Larrikin humour and egalitarian "mateship" are prized.
society: Iron ore, coal and gas exports, much of them to China, power the economy, which avoided recession for nearly three decades. Housing has become among the world's least affordable. A 2023 referendum to create an Indigenous Voice to Parliament was defeated. The AUKUS pact will give Australia nuclear-powered submarines.
situation: In 1998, Pauline Hanson, a former fish-and-chip shop owner who warned that Australia was being "swamped by Asians," won nearly a quarter of the vote in Queensland and shocked the political establishment. Her One Nation party then faded for years into a fringe. In 2026, it came roaring back, and the party that suffered most was not the governing Labor Party but the conservative Liberals, Australia's natural party of government for most of its history.

After a crushing loss in 2025, the Liberals' coalition with the Nationals split and their vote fell below One Nation's. In February, Angus Taylor, a former McKinsey consultant, ousted Sussan Ley as Liberal leader (Spectator Australia). It barely helped. By June, a Resolve poll had more voters preferring Hanson as prime minister (33 percent) than Anthony Albanese (29), with Taylor on 16; a Liberal frontbencher admitted "we have broken faith with the Australian people" (Neos Kosmos/AAP). One Nation's support dipped after Hanson told the National Press Club Australia should be a "monoculture," but by August a RedBridge poll had it back in first place on 31 percent (AAP via Mudgee Guardian). In July, Taylor ruled out any alliance, warning a One Nation government would bring "an eternity of pain" (The New Daily). Albanese's own ratings have sagged over living costs and the return of so-called "ISIS brides" from Syria. Under Australia's preferential voting, Labor still leads head-to-head, but the country's two-party system is cracking.
power: A parliamentary democracy and Commonwealth realm. The prime minister leads the party with a majority in the 150-seat House of Representatives, elected by preferential voting; the Senate is elected proportionally and often decides legislation. Voting is compulsory.
holders: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese (Labor), in office since 2022; next election due by 2028.
